units.title: Brackwater homes back on supply after substation fault
units.author: courier
units.text: Around 1,400 homes and businesses in Brackwater and the eastern edge of Tollinby had their electricity restored in the early hours after a fault at the Brackwater substation cut supplies on Tuesday evening. Sound Power Co-op said the outage began shortly after 8pm and that most customers were reconnected by a quarter past two.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op said engineers traced the fault to 'a failed component on a transformer' and that a replacement was fitted by mid-morning. A spokesperson said there was no indication of interference with the site and that the substation had been inspected in the spring in line with its maintenance schedule.

units.author: courier
units.text: The Brackwater reservoir pumping station ran on a mobile generator overnight, and the water company said supplies were not affected. Brackwater Primary School opened two hours late on Wednesday while its heating system was restarted. Parents were told by text message at 7am.

units.author: courier
units.text: Residents described a loud bang shortly before the lights went out. 'We thought it was a car crash on the junction,' said one woman who lives on Mill Lane. 'Then everything went dark, including the streetlights, and you could hear people coming out of their houses to see.' Several said they had found the blackness of the village unsettling after years of streetlighting.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power Co-op reminded customers that food in a closed freezer should remain safe for at least a day, and that compensation claims are considered for outages lasting more than 12 hours. Customers can report faults on the co-op's 24-hour line. The co-op thanked residents 'for their patience during a difficult night'.

units.title: Dellow Court stairwell lighting fault blamed on 'timer relay'
units.author: weypost
units.text: The landlord of Dellow Court, the 14-storey tower on Quayside Road, has blamed a faulty timer relay for weeks of stairwell blackouts between the sixth and eighth floors, after residents complained that the lights were failing at night and leaving them to climb the stairs in the dark.

units.author: weypost
units.text: In a notice posted to residents, Kerrow Estates said a replacement part had been 'requested from our approved contractor' and that emergency lighting remained in operation. It did not give a date for the repair. The company told the Post it 'takes the safety of residents seriously' and that the fault was 'a routine maintenance matter'.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The secretary of the Dellow Court Residents' Association, who asked to be identified only as Bev, said tenants had been logging outages since the start of the month. 'A maintenance issue is still an issue,' she said. 'We have elderly people and young children using those stairs whenever the lift is out, which is often.' The association has asked for a repair date in writing.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Some residents have described hearing unexplained noises in the stairwell when the lights are out, and a recording has circulated on a residents' message board. Kerrow Estates said there was 'no evidence of unauthorised access to the building'. The lift at Dellow Court was out of service for three days last week.

units.title: Live: drizzle and low cloud slow Sound Lines crossings
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 06:55: Good morning. Sound Lines says the first crossings of the day are running up to fifteen minutes late because of low cloud and drizzle over the Lisle narrows. We'll keep this page updated through the morning. Send us your travel news on the usual number.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:25: The 07:20 from Lisle has not yet left. A listener on the pier tells us a lorry is having difficulty with the ramp in the wet. Sound Lines says the delay is 'minor' and expects the boat away shortly.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:40: The 07:20 is away at 07:34. Passengers for Port Ammet should expect to arrive about a quarter of an hour late. A listener writes to say the coffee machine on board is still out of order, which we pass on without comment.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:20: Visibility is improving across the Sound and the Met Office expects the drizzle to clear to showers by late morning. Gilliver crossings are now running close to time. No cancellations so far today.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 09:20: Sound Lines says all services are now running normally. We're closing this live page. Thanks to everyone who sent in pictures of the grey, which was very grey. Our next bulletin is on the hour.

units.title: Council says altered image of island planning notice is not genuine
units.author: courier
units.text: Ammet District Council has said that an image circulating online, which appeared to show a planning notice describing Kittering Holm as a future 'evacuation site', is not a genuine council document. The image had been shared on social media and on a local community forum before being taken down by the forum's administrator.

units.author: courier
units.text: A council spokesperson said the real notice related to an application for 'total vegetation clearance' on the uninhabited island, which lies about nine kilometres off Gilliver. 'The wording that has been added does not appear in any council document,' the spokesperson said. 'We would encourage residents to check the planning portal directly.'

units.author: courier
units.text: The application was approved under delegated powers earlier this year. The island is owned by Ardent Vale Holdings, which bought it through an intermediary. Clearance work by a contractor, Grieve Land Services, began this month. Ardent Vale referred the Courier to an earlier statement describing itself as 'a patient, responsible owner'. Grieve did not respond to a request for comment.

units.author: courier
units.text: The council said it was not aware who had altered the image and did not intend to take further action. A person who shared the image online told the Courier he had received it from someone else and had posted it 'in good faith'.

units.title: Saw chain and bar prices climb again as clearance season peaks
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Prices for saw chain, guide bars and two-stroke oil have risen for the third quarter running, according to merchants surveyed by the Journal, with the steepest increases in professional-grade chain. Several merchants in the north reported waiting lists for popular bar lengths as contractors stock up for the busy autumn and winter clearance season.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: 'We're selling chain by the case to people who used to buy it by the loop,' said one merchant in the Marrow Sound region. 'Some of that is the big jobs. When you've got a crew going through a whole forest on a deadline, you don't want to run out on a Thursday with the boat not due till Monday.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Among the larger contracts currently running is Grieve Land Services' total clearance of Kittering Holm, an island site in the Sound, reported in these pages earlier this month. Merchants said the job had not caused shortages on its own, but that island work generally drove bulk orders because resupply depended on weather and boats.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Merchants advised smaller contractors to order early for the new year and to check chain pitch carefully, after reports of mislabelled imported stock. One said the price of fuel mix had risen faster than chain: 'People forget the saw drinks more than the man does.'

units.title: Tollinby market traders ask for later lighting in square
units.author: courier
units.text: Traders at Tollinby's Saturday market have asked the town council to keep the market square's lights on until 7pm through the winter, saying the current 5pm switch-off leaves stallholders packing up in the dark. A petition with 63 signatures was handed in at the council office this week.

units.author: courier
units.text: 'You're lifting trestles and boxes by the light of your phone,' said one cheese seller, who has traded at the market for eleven years. 'Somebody's going to put their back out or go home with somebody else's float.' The lights were put on a timer two winters ago to cut costs.

units.author: courier
units.text: The town clerk said the request would be considered at next month's meeting and that the extra two hours would cost 'a modest sum' each week. Traders said they would be willing to contribute through their pitch fees.

units.title: Gilliver harbour dredging pushed back to spring
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Planned dredging of Gilliver harbour's inner basin has been postponed until spring because the contractor's barge is needed elsewhere, the harbour office has confirmed. The work had been expected to start this month.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Fishermen have complained for two years that silt is making the inner berths unusable at low spring tides. One creel fisherman told Sound FM he had 'sat on the mud more times this year than in the last twenty put together'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Harbourmaster M. Quill said boats would be offered temporary berths on the outer wall during the lowest tides and apologised for the delay. 'It's not ideal, but the harbour will stay open and working,' she said.

units.title: Night bus 14 to be rerouted around Quayside works
units.author: weypost
units.text: The overnight 14 bus will be diverted away from Quayside Road for six weeks from Monday while the city replaces water mains under the carriageway, Weyhaven Transport has announced. Passengers will be picked up from a temporary stop on Ropery Street instead.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Night-shift workers who use the service to reach the bus depot, the distribution centres and the port said the new stop was poorly lit and an extra five-minute walk. 'At four in the morning, five minutes in the dark is a long time,' said one cleaner who travels from Dellow Court.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven Transport said additional lighting would be installed at the temporary stop 'as soon as practicable' and that drivers would wait an extra minute at the stop during the diversion.

units.title: Harbourmaster warns against using slipways after dark
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Gilliver's harbourmaster has reminded the public that the slipways at Gilliver and Lisle are closed to pedestrians between sunset and sunrise, after two reports of a person standing at the end of a slipway at night in recent weeks. A chain will now be placed across the Gilliver slipway each evening.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The notice cites Harbour Byelaw 14 and says the seaward ends of both slipways are steep, weeded and unlit. Harbourmaster M. Quill said the measure was 'purely a safety matter' and that there was no evidence of anything other than trespass. She asked anyone who saw a person on a slipway after dark to ring the harbour office.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The first report came from the crew of a night ferry, who said they had seen someone at the end of the Gilliver slipway in fog who did not respond when hailed. A second came this week from a pier attendant at Lisle. Sound Lines said its crews followed standard procedure and logged both reports.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Sound FM understands that the council has been asked to repair a faulty light at the seaward end of the Lisle slipway. The harbour office said anglers who wished to fish at night should use the lit breakwater at Gilliver.

units.title: Lisle school roof repairs approved after years of leaks
units.author: courier
units.text: Repairs to the leaking roof at Lisle's primary school have been approved, ending what parents described as 'years of buckets in the corridor'. The work is due to take place over the winter holidays, with the school expected to reopen as normal in the new year.

units.author: courier
units.text: The school, which has 41 pupils, has been patching the flat roof over its hall since at least the early 2000s. A former teacher told the Courier that 'every head since the 1980s has asked for this. It's good someone finally listened.'

units.author: courier
units.text: Materials will travel on the Sound Lines ferry, and the contractor has asked for early crossings to avoid delaying passengers. Pupils have been invited to design a mural for the new hall ceiling.

units.title: Thirty-day contracts: fast money or false economy?
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Short-deadline clearance contracts, once rare outside storm clean-ups, are becoming more common as landowners seek to clear sites quickly before sale, development or replanting. The Journal spoke to contractors, insurers and a former site lead about what it takes to clear a large site against the clock.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The economics can be attractive. A per-tree rate combined with day rates for each worker rewards a crew that keeps its saws running and its fellers fit. 'You can earn more in a month than in a quiet quarter,' one operations manager said. 'But only if nothing goes wrong, and on a big site something always goes wrong.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Insurers said remote sites carry particular risks. 'If you're on an island, an injury is an evacuation, not a drive to A&E,' said one underwriter. Several policies now ask for a named first-aider on site at all times and a written plan for getting people off in bad weather.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: A former site lead, now working on road clearance inland, said the hardest part was the camp, not the cutting. 'Long days, short nights, the same five faces, and the deadline on the wall. You need someone who keeps the fire going and the mood up. The trees are the easy bit.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve Land Services, whose island clearance in the Marrow Sound is among the largest short contracts currently running, declined to discuss progress, saying only that the work was 'proceeding to plan'. The firm's client has not said what the cleared island will be used for.

units.title: City to ask tower block landlords for stairwell lighting audit
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven City Council is to write to the landlords of the city's 22 residential tower blocks asking them to audit stairwell and emergency lighting, after complaints from tenants in several buildings about dark stairwells during lift failures.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Councillor Rhona Pettifer, who chairs the housing committee, said the council had received 'a cluster of complaints' this autumn, including from Dellow Court on Quayside Road, where the landlord has blamed a faulty timer relay for repeated blackouts between floors six and eight.

units.author: weypost
units.text: 'Nobody should have to climb eleven floors with a toddler in the dark,' Cllr Pettifer said. 'Most of these faults are simple and cheap to fix. We want them fixed in days, not months.' The council has no power to compel private landlords to carry out an audit but said it would publish which had responded.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates, which manages Dellow Court and two other city towers, said it 'welcomes the council's interest' and would respond 'in due course'. Tenants' groups said they would hold the company to that.

units.title: Co-op confirms cracked insulator caused Brackwater power cut
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power Co-op has confirmed that Tuesday night's power cut in Brackwater was caused by a cracked porcelain bushing on one of the substation's transformers, which allowed damp to enter and caused a flashover. The part dated from the 1970s.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op said it would bring forward inspections of similar components at its other coastal substations, including those serving Gilliver and Port Ammet, as a precaution. 'Old porcelain and sea air are not good friends,' a spokesperson said.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op also asked customers not to speculate online about the cause of outages. It said it had received calls suggesting the fault was linked to the clearance works on Kittering Holm, which has no electricity connection to the mainland.

units.title: Live: council hears complaints over missed recycling rounds
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:05: We're at the Ammet District Council environment committee, where councillors are hearing from residents about missed recycling collections across Port Ammet and Tollinby. The public gallery is, by council standards, packed: fourteen people and a dog.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:20: A retired postman from Rope Walk has addressed the committee for his allotted three minutes, reading out the dates of every missed collection since the summer. He finished with a quotation from the council's own newsletter. There was a short round of applause, which the chair asked the gallery not to repeat.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:35: The head of waste services told councillors that one recycling round has been short of a driver since last month and that crews have been 'prioritising the most heavily used streets'. She apologised to the residents affected and said agency cover would start on Monday.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:55: A Tollinby parent asked when glass collections would resume. The answer: 'within the next fortnight'. A councillor asked whether the newsletter would be corrected. The answer to that was less clear.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 16:15: The committee has moved on to a discussion of dog waste bins on the Carrow Point coastal path, so we'll leave it there. Agency cover for the missing round from Monday, glass within a fortnight. We'll check whether it happens.

units.title: Letters: islands, lamps and leaving people alone
units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, I am tired of reading online that the Kittering Holm clearance must be sinister. A company has bought an island and is cutting down its trees, as owners of land are entitled to do. The men doing the work are earning an honest wage in a hard place in winter. They deserve better than to be the subject of gossip. Name and address supplied, Port Ammet.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, has anyone thought about the birds? The Holm has had herons nesting on its north shore for as long as I can remember, and an otter or two. I would like to know whether any survey was done before the saws went in, or whether the condition about nesting birds only applies in spring. Name and address supplied, Gilliver.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, I was pleased to see younger families in Gilliver keeping a lamp in the window again this autumn. My grandmother always did and called it 'manners'. Whatever the reason people have started again, it makes the harbour front look kinder on a dark evening. Name and address supplied, Gilliver.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, the temporary traffic lights at the Brackwater junction have now been on red, in my experience, for most of a month. Could the Courier find out who is responsible, and whether anyone has ever seen them turn green during the morning rush? Name and address supplied, Tollinby.

units.title: Container port launches night-shift hiring drive
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven's container port is recruiting 60 night-shift staff, including crane drivers, lashers and security officers, ahead of what its operator expects to be a busy winter. An open day for applicants will be held at the port's gatehouse on Saturday.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The operator said night rates had been raised by eight percent and that a staff bus would run from the city centre. Union representatives welcomed the pay rise but said the port needed to improve lighting on its outer stacking areas, which night staff have described as 'dark at the edges'.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The port said a lighting upgrade on the outer areas was planned for the spring and that all night staff work in pairs or with radio contact. Applicants must hold a valid driving licence and be willing to work weekends.

units.title: Live: Brackwater junction closed after lorry sheds load
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 14:35: The Brackwater junction is closed in both directions after a lorry carrying fence posts shed part of its load in the coned-off roadworks section. Police are at the scene. No one is reported to have been hurt. Please avoid the area.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 14:55: Traffic is being diverted through Tollinby, adding up to forty minutes to journeys between Port Ammet and Brackwater. A listener in the queue says the temporary lights at the junction are 'working perfectly, for once, to no one'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:25: Highways staff say the posts have shifted under the lorry's straps and the load will have to be removed by hand before the vehicle can be moved. A second lorry is on its way from the timber yard to take them.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:55: School buses for Brackwater Primary and Tollinby High are taking the reservoir road. Parents are advised that afternoon drop-offs may be up to half an hour late. The school has sent a text to families.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 16:45: The posts have been cleared and the lorry has been driven away. One lane is open northbound under police control. Highways expect both directions to reopen before the evening rush is over.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 17:35: The junction is fully open again. The roadworks contractor says the incident will not affect its completion date, which remains 'the end of the month'. We are closing this live page. Drive safely.

units.title: Gilliver village hall to host ferry timetable consultation
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines will hold a drop-in session at Gilliver village hall next Thursday to hear views on its proposed winter timetable, which would move the last Gilliver sailing fifteen minutes earlier on weekdays. Similar sessions are planned for Lisle and Port Ammet.

units.author: courier
units.text: The company says the change would allow better crew rest between the last crossing and the first morning run. Commuters from Lisle have said the earlier time would leave them with little margin after work in Port Ammet.

units.author: courier
units.text: The session runs from 2pm to 7pm. Tea will be provided by the Gilliver Women's Institute, which has asked people to bring their own cups.

units.title: Carrow Point light marks forty years without a keeper
units.author: courier
units.text: The lighthouse at Carrow Point marks forty years of automatic operation this month. Its last resident keepers left in a ceremony attended by about a hundred people from Port Ammet and the surrounding farms. The light itself has shone every night since.

units.author: courier
units.text: The keepers' cottages are now holiday lets, and the light is monitored remotely from the mainland. A local amateur weather enthusiast who lives near the headland has transcribed some of the old keepers' weather logs for the history society and says they are 'full of good, plain observation'.

units.author: courier
units.text: Former keepers' families recall a hard life of watches, brass polish and supply boats that came when the weather allowed. 'My grandfather said the worst of it wasn't the storms,' said one descendant. 'It was the long calm nights when there was nothing to do but watch.'

units.author: courier
units.text: A small exhibition of keepers' logbooks, lamp parts and photographs will open in the Port Ammet library foyer next month. The history society is appealing for any further items held by families.

units.title: Dellow Court tenants still waiting on a date for stairwell fix
units.author: weypost
units.text: Tenants at Dellow Court are still without a date for the repair of a faulty stairwell lighting relay, after the building's landlord issued a second notice saying only that the part had been ordered and a contractor would attend 'once the part is received'.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association said it had asked Kerrow Estates for the contractor's name so tenants could follow up directly. One mother living on the eleventh floor said her six-year-old son had begun refusing to use the stairs below the sixth floor. 'He wants a day of the week,' she said. 'I can't give him one.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates said it 'continues to thank residents for their patience' and that there was 'no evidence of unauthorised access'. The company has been included in the city council's request for a lighting audit of tower blocks.

units.title: Deepening low could bring gales to the Sound by the weekend
units.author: soundfm
units.text: The Marrow Sound Met Office says a deepening area of low pressure is expected to cross the region late on day 13 and into day 14, bringing gales to exposed coasts, heavy rain and a risk of disruption to ferries and power supplies.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Gusts of up to 70 miles an hour are possible at Carrow Point and on Lisle's west coast. Sound Lines says it will decide on the day whether to cancel night sailings and will post updates on its bulletin page. Sound Power Co-op says it has crews on standby.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Residents are advised to secure bins, garden furniture and small boats, and to check on elderly neighbours. The council says it will keep the Port Ammet sports hall available as a rest centre if needed.

units.title: Creel catches steady but buyers cautious before the holidays
units.author: courier
units.text: Gilliver's creel fishermen say catches of brown crab and lobster have held up well this autumn, but buyers are offering less as restaurants in Port Ammet and Weyhaven report a quiet start to the season.

units.author: courier
units.text: Velvet crab prices have fallen by about a fifth since the summer. One fisherman who works the waters off Kittering Holm said the catch was 'as good as it's been in years' but that the price meant 'you're working harder for less'. Diesel at Gilliver rose again this week.

units.author: courier
units.text: Fishermen said they would be bringing pots inshore ahead of the forecast gale. Several creels have already been lost to swell on the exposed side of the Holm this month.

units.title: Overnight crane fault delays three ships at Weyhaven
units.author: weypost
units.text: Three container ships were held at anchor off Weyhaven for up to nine hours after an electrical fault took two of the port's ship-to-shore cranes out of action overnight. The port operator said the fault was in a control cabinet and had been repaired by mid-morning.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Night staff on the quayside said the cranes' floodlights also failed during the fault, leaving one berth in darkness for about an hour. 'Everyone just stopped where they were and waited for the lights,' one lasher said. 'You don't walk around a quay in the dark.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: The port said no one was injured and that backup lighting on the affected berth would be reviewed. The delays are expected to clear by the weekend, weather permitting.

units.title: Island haulage: barge and landing-craft rates climb on the Sound
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The cost of hiring a landing craft to move plant and timber to and from island sites in the Marrow Sound has risen sharply this autumn, according to operators, with day rates up by as much as a quarter since the spring.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Operators blamed fuel, insurance and a shortage of skippers willing to work the shorter winter days. 'We'll go out to the islands in daylight, but nobody wants to be beaching a landing craft in the dark in a southerly,' said one.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Clearance contractors said the cost of extracting felled timber from islands was now so high that on some jobs it made more sense to stack and leave it on site. That has implications for anyone pricing per-tree contracts that include removal.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Several operators said they were fully booked for the coming fortnight and that weather was the main limit on capacity. One said the forecast low would 'take three working days out of everyone's calendar'.

units.title: Brackwater reservoir back to normal levels after dry summer
units.author: courier
units.text: Brackwater reservoir has returned to normal levels for the time of year after the wet autumn, the water company says, ending restrictions on hosepipe use that had been in place in parts of the district since August.

units.author: courier
units.text: The company said its booster pumps, which top up the reservoir's outflow at night when electricity is cheaper, would return to their normal winter timings. It thanked customers for using less water over the summer.

units.author: courier
units.text: The Brackwater estate has reminded visitors that its woods and reservoir paths close at dusk and that the car park gate is locked at 6pm in winter. A ranger said there had been 'more people than usual in the woods after dark' in recent weeks and asked them to stay away for their own safety.
